metadata.title: Reform UK plays down crypto ties as it courts business, diplomats

content.text:
Investing.com -- Reform UK is reducing the prominence of cryptocurrency companies at its annual conference as Nigel Farage's party seeks to strengthen its credentials with businesses and foreign governments, Bloomberg reported Saturday.
No crypto companies appear on the latest sponsor list for next week's three-day conference in Birmingham, a shift from last year when digital payments company Zebec was a prominent backer.
Benefits previously offered to the crypto industry, including free tickets and access to senior Reform officials, have also been reduced, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The shift comes as Farage faces a parliamentary investigation into whether he should have declared £5 million ($6.8 million) received from Thailand-based crypto investor Christopher Harborne.
Reform is instead seeking to highlight growing engagement with international governments and major businesses as it tries to position itself as a potential party of government.
Representatives from nearly a dozen countries are expected to attend, honorary treasurer Nick Candy told Bloomberg. India, Italy, Hungary, Poland, the UAE and U.S. are among countries expected to send ambassadors or other representatives.
French National Rally leader Jordan Bardella is also scheduled to speak.
Reform will hold its first business day on Thursday, with companies including construction group Keltbray, equipment manufacturer JCB, TikTok and Heathrow Airport expected to attend alongside major technology firms.
More than 600 tickets have been sold for the business event, Bloomberg reported. Full-price tickets cost £495, with a separate evening dinner priced at £395.
Reform currently holds eight seats in Britain's 650-seat House of Commons but has sought to position itself as a contender for power at the next general election, due by 2029.
Its rise has recently faced pressure from a recovery in support for the governing Labour Party. Labour has drawn level with Reform since Prime Minister Andy Burnham took office in July, according to Bloomberg's average of opinion polls.
